newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares tread water ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares tread water ahead of FOMC.

text.p: Austrian shares ended marginally lower in sluggish trade on Tuesday and dealers said the market was in wait-and-see mode ahead of the outcome of a key FOMC meeting.
The ATX of 21 blue-chip shares slipped 0.21 points, or 0.02 percent, to 1,215.48 and never seriously threatened to break out of a 1,210 to 1,220 points trading range.
April ATX futures were up 3.5 points at 1,217.5 on turnover of 610 contracts.
"We did nothing but wait around today," a dealer said.

A 0.25 percentage point increase in U.S. interest rates was already factored into Austrian share prices, a second market participant said, adding: "Unless the Fed springs a surprise on us, I see prices pretty much rangebound."
Limited trading interest focused on Vienna airport company Flughafen Wien and steelmaker VA Stahl.

Flughafen remained under selling pressure for the second day, despite the firm's denial late on Monday that one of its two chief executives had resigned. Flughafen shares closed 14 schillings down at 535 on volume of 57,680.
VA Stahl was one of the few sought-after shares, climbing 7.3 schillings to 478.5 on 84,872 lots.
"Apart from those two stocks today was eminently forgettable," a trader said.
Overall 12 ATX shares were lower, eight higher and one unchanged.
Top gainer was fireproof materials manufacturer Radex-Heraklith, which releases 1996 earnings data on Wednesday. Its shares firmed 3.05 percent to 439 schillings.
Semi-conductor maker AMS was the leading decliner, down 3.25 percent to 1,071 schillings.
In second line trade BWT, maker of water treatment technology, rose one schilling to 1,400 after the firm provided more details of its newest technology.
